newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-History put up for sale in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-History put up for sale in Australia.

text.p: One of the world's biggest private collections of cricket memorabilia has been auctioned by Christie's in Australia, with the 1902 pocket-sized diary of Australian batsman Victor Trumper fetching A$29,900 (US$22,125).

English collector John McKenzie flew to Australia especially for the Sunday night auction and snared the diary written by Trumper during the 1902 Ashes tour of England when he scored 11 centuries. Trumper played 48 tests for Australia.
McKenzie narrowly missed out on Trumper's 1899 green velvet Australian cap, which went to an undisclosed buyer for A$28,750.

McKenzie also paid A$10,000 for a bat used by Australian player Clem Hill in 1897-98, while other items among the 400 sold included a pair of Trumper's cufflinks and a blazer worn by Australia all-rounder Doug Walters.
"We have had big sales overseas but this is certainly one of the biggest single collections in the world," Christie's spokeswoman Julie King said.
"There were bidders from England and we were led to believe that some members of the Australian side were among the bidders, although we can't disclose names," King said.
The owner of the unique collection of cricket memorabilia said on Monday he had succumbed to family pressure in agreeing to an auction of his beloved pieces which netted over A$400,000.
"My daughter and my wife were not that keen to continue," said Indian-born cricket fanatic Srikantan Ramamurthy, who has lived in Australia for the past 34 years.
"I'm at such an age where I've stopped collecting and once you stop collecting, it's hard to maintain interest," Ramamurthy told Reuters.

Ramamurthy, 58, said he and his family had spent most of their annual holidays for the past 35 years travelling the world in search of cricket memorabilia. His collection became so big it was difficult to house under one roof. (A$1 = US$0.74)
